statement: For p-dimensional polynomial spaces in C[z]≤m+p−1, the complex Wronski map has degree d(m,p)=(mp)!·∏_(j=1)^(p−1)j!/∏_(j=0)^(p−1)(m+j)!. Thus a generic projective Wronskian has exactly this many preimages.

source.location: Theorem A, equation (4), printed p. 3; Wronski specialization (6), printed p. 4

notes:
Theorem A is credited to Schubert; the paper identifies the Wronski map as a central projection with center disjoint from the Grassmannian. This is the degree of that projection, not an unsupported substitution of variety degree.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_3b265d2296311021; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

Eremenko–Gabrielov explicitly credit this complex degree to Schubert’s 1886 computation. Their realization of the Wronski map as a central projection is retained in the source; their new real topological degree has its own record.
